meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тоять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'stop, wait', paired with 'постоять'.

examples.trans: Congratulations, daddy, a real bouncing boy.
I'm standing here.

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

meanings.en: to give away, to hand over
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'give', paired with 'отдавать'.

examples.trans: Stop, hand over the bag!
Security, give back my bag!
Give me the keys.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'умка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'bag, handbag' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Слушай, я забыла сумку, я быстро.
examples.trans: Listen, I forgot my bag, I will be quick.
Stop, hand over the bag!
What is going on, this is my bag!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!
The main thing is that I am here.

examples.text: Тем более, что ты уже начал.
examples.trans: Especially since you have already started.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'such, like this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You have such a wonderful boss.

examples.text: Так сбежал, что ты до него не доберёшься.
examples.trans: He ran so far that you will not reach him.

examples.text: У чувака на форуме такая же проблема.
examples.trans: A guy on the forum has the exact same problem.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
This is not your child.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Но я точно знаю, что ребёнок мой.
examples.trans: But I know for sure that the child is mine.

examples.text: Дело в том, что это мой ребёнок.
examples.trans: The thing is that this is my child.
My first husband is Victor Petrovich.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'security' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Security, give back my bag!
Call security!
Security is at the door.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You have such a wonderful boss.

examples.text: Так сбежал, что ты до него не доберёшься.
examples.trans: He ran so far that you will not reach him.

examples.text: У чувака на форуме такая же проблема.
examples.trans: A guy on the forum has the exact same problem.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'happened', paired with 'случаться'.

examples.trans: What happened?
Nothing will happen.

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'hands' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Take your hands off me!
Give me your hand.
I shake your hand! (a goodbye)

meanings.en: to remove, to take away, to cut out
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'брать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'take away / remove', paired with 'убирать'.

examples.text: Ты можешь убрать весь этот шум?
examples.trans: Can you cut out all this noise?
Take the phone off the table.

examples.text: Так, ты можешь убрать весь этот шум? Нам нужен только Аникеев.
examples.trans: Right, can you cut out all this noise? We only need Anikeev.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
Work does not wait, it is time to run.
Do you want to ruin our relationship?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The rookie has returned!
I know that you are pregnant!
The main thing is that I am here.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Лена, а кто автор всех этих шедевров?
examples.trans: Lena, and who is the author of all these masterpieces?
Quiet, quiet, what on earth is happening?
Quiet, the children are asleep!

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.text: Вообще-то у нас обедает финский посол.
examples.trans: Actually, the Finnish ambassador is having lunch with us.

examples.text: А Костя вообще врать не умеет.
examples.trans: And Kostya does not know how to lie at all.
Quiet, quiet, what on earth is happening?

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'исходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is happening', paired with 'произойти'.

examples.trans: Quiet, quiet, what on earth is happening?
What is going on? I don't understand.
What is happening here?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Are you two chatting here?

examples.text: А я вот себе туфли новые купил.
examples.trans: And I just bought myself new shoes.

examples.text: Вы с Викой расстались, и она сразу кого-то нашла?
examples.trans: You and Vika broke up, and she immediately found someone?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
That simply cannot be!
I have a toy car.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овершенно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: You were completely right.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.
This is a completely new car.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('right').

examples.text: Кате всё равно правду не расскажешь.
examples.trans: You cannot tell Katya the truth anyway.

examples.text: Это какую правду Кате не расскажешь?
examples.trans: What truth can you not tell Katya?

examples.text: Моя команда справится с послом и без меня.
examples.trans: My team will handle the ambassador without me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: She is a good one you have.
Calm down, I will leave everything to a professional.
Maybe she was joking?

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'ровка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'thief' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She is a thief!

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть воровка.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always thief.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'пустить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'let go, release', paired with 'отпускать'.

examples.trans: Did they not let him out of the asylum?
Let her go, this is a misunderstanding.
Release him immediately!

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'доразумение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'misunderstanding' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Let her go, this is a misunderstanding.
There was a terrible misunderstanding this morning.
It's just a misunderstanding.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you, Nastya!
Thank you, everything is very delicious.
Thank you for your vigilance.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Who told you?

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.
You have such a wonderful boss.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'vigilance' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you for your vigilance.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть бдительность.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always vigilance.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ъяснить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'explain', paired with 'объяснять'.

examples.text: Витя, объясни мне, что это значит!
examples.trans: Vitya, explain to me what this means!
I'll explain everything later.
Explain, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А это значит ярко и красочно.
examples.trans: And this means brightly and colorfully.

examples.text: Витя, объясни мне, что это значит!
examples.trans: Vitya, explain to me what this means!
So she told the truth.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: And where is the daughter right now?
I will do everything right now, Chef.

examples.text: Ты побудь здесь, я сейчас с ней поговорю.
examples.trans: You stay here, I will go talk to her right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Calm down, I will leave everything to a professional.

examples.text: Кате всё равно правду не расскажешь.
examples.trans: You cannot tell Katya the truth anyway.
Alright, it is settled, we are going.
